answer: One concrete Sybil defense is economic stake bonding: an agent must lock scarce collateral to earn a single identity, and misbehavior triggers slashing. To mint a fake identity the attacker pays the full bond up front, so a thousand clones require a thousand bonds, while honest agents risk the same capital. Detection turns each forged ember into a real loss; the scarce opal collateral is burned, leaving the attacker no safe haven to hide behind. Because each identity is priced in real value, scaling an attack scales the cost linearly, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
